about: The recording script of the Meridian help videos: one tour per guide chapter, read by e2e/guided-tours-v2.spec.ts (RECORD_HELP=1, the recording project). Every step shows its caption, then does its action (go, click, point, press, fill, focus), then holds long enough to read. The captions are the videos' subtitle track and are searched by the help panel.

steps.caption: Meridian checks your SAP data against fixed rules and scores every object on every system.
The Demo data bar says these figures are sample data. A customer installation never shows it.
Three surfaces: the map of systems and objects on the left, the canvas in the middle, the inspector on the right.
The landscape is the start screen. One sentence says what holds the data back.
Every cell is a small ruler: the shown score, the word capped, the measured score beside it, and the verdict.
The next-step button is shaped for your role. For a programme lead it follows the nearest wave.
Open Material master on ECC production.
The ruler: six segments sized by the dimension weights, each filled to its score.
Measured 71.8, the tick on the ruler. Capped at 70 by MM003 and MM035, two critical rules over tolerance.
The receipt adds the score up, dimension by dimension, then the cap and the score shown.
The tabs sit under the title: rules, records, fixes, runs, readiness, processes, lineage, glossary, golden records.
Rules are ranked by value at risk, each with what goes wrong in SAP while it fails.
Select a rule and it opens in the inspector, beside the canvas.
Esc closes the inspector and returns you to where you were.
Work is the ledger: every failing record and field on one row, with the fix on the row.
Current value, suggested value, new value and the decision sit beside the rule. Possible values are in the column chooser.
The chips filter by state: to fix, fix proposed, waiting for approval, exceptions.
Every fix waits in a batch for a second person. Four eyes has no bypass.
Runs: every measurement on one timeline, with the baseline marked.
Compare two runs and Meridian says why each score moved.
People: who holds the open work, what waits for approval, and the SLA.
Press Command K, or slash, to open the command line.
Type a rule id, a material number, an object, or a word such as approve.

fill.label: Search, ask, or type a command

steps.caption: Enter opens the result.
Help is the question mark in the top bar: the chapter for this screen comes first.
Every number has its receipt. Nothing is guessed: every figure is a rule result over stored data.
The landscape: every system and object with its score.
The sentence says what holds the landscape back, and which rules would release objects if fixed.
Records checked, rules measured and the run the figures come from.
The next-step button: one per role. Here, the no-go objects of the nearest wave.
Each cell reads like 70.0 capped, 71.8 measured: the shown score, and the measured score the objects are ranked by.
A system never extracted says so, with the action that fixes it.
Plant maintenance is flagged low coverage: fewer than 70% of its rules produced a result.
Your next work: the top rows of the ledger, ranked by value at risk.
The footer names the run, the cost model and any failed job. Every amount is an estimate from the cost model.
Switch to Waves to group the objects under each migration wave.
A data steward sees the same landscape with a different next step.
SAP Basis gets its own home above the matrix: connections, extractions, failed jobs, authorisation errors and schedules.
An address Meridian does not know says so, instead of showing a page that looks real.
Open any cell to read the object behind it.
An object is one area of SAP data scored as a whole on one system.
The tabs sit under the title. The Rules view comes first and carries the receipt.
The facts line: run, records checked, rules measured, records to fix, value at risk marked est., features blocked, wave verdict.
Related objects, upstream and downstream. Fix upstream first.
The ruler: the tick is the measured score, the number is the score shown. It reads 70.0 capped, 71.8 measured.
Capped at 70 by MM003 and MM035: two critical rules over tolerance.
The receipt: each dimension's weight, score and points, then measured, cap and score shown.
Every i explains its figure from the run itself.
Rules, ranked by value at risk, with tolerance and whether each is over it.
Pivot the rules by field, dimension, severity or S/4 feature.
Runs: the measured score over eight runs, and why it moved against the baseline.
The shown score moved only to 70.0, because the cap holds it.
Readiness: the waves this object is in, and what its failing rules block in S/4HANA.
Fixes lists the object's fix batches.
Watch the object to hear about runs, score drops and new critical breaches.
A rule is a fixed check with an id, a field, a dimension and a severity.
MM142 is a high rule: failing records across objects, the share, the estimated value at risk, within tolerance, features blocked.
Definition: the check class, the field as MARA-MEINS, the expression and the authority.
Versions: who changed the rule, when and why.
Scope: every object and system the rule runs on, with its failing count.
The rule inspector holds the same facts beside any canvas. MM003 is one of the two critical rules that cap Material master.
Tolerance: only critical rules carry one. Over it, the rule caps the score.
Comment on the rule, and watch it.
The rules library lists every rule of the tenant: 794 across 15 objects, every page of them.
Filter by object, dimension, severity, check class and state.
Drafts run nowhere until they are reviewed and enabled.
New rule draft starts a rule in authoring.
Work is the ledger: every failing record and field, ranked by value at risk.
The chips are the filter: to fix, fix proposed, waiting for approval, exceptions.
Each row holds the current value, the suggested value, the new value and the decision. Possible values are in the column chooser.
Choose a decision: fix, not an issue or accept risk.
Every change shows a notice with Undo.
Command Z takes the last change back.
Select rows with x or the checkboxes; Shift J extends the selection.
The bulk bar acts on every selected row.
A change of more than 25 rows waits on a confirmation bar with the count.
Enter confirms; Escape keeps the rows as they are.
By rule groups the rows under their rule, so a whole rule is decided at once.
Open a record: every failing field, its possible values and the decision.
Feature impact, provenance and history are on the record too.
Export fix sheet saves the rows on screen to Excel, with the same columns.
Fill it in offline and import it back: Meridian checks keys, fields and values before anything changes.
Share and export saves a view, exports any grid, or shares the page as a read-only link.
Every value decided in Work waits in a fix batch until a second person approves it.
Rows are grouped by batch, with who built it, the records, value at risk and the due date.
Open the batch for its facts, its changes and the approval trail.
Each change reads as the SAP field and the pair of values.
You cover for a colleague who is away: their approvals come to you as well.
The approval trail: who drafted the batch and who proposed the values.
Approve acts on the whole batch. Send back asks for a reason the steward reads.
Approval does not touch SAP. The batch is exported and loaded; the next run confirms each record.
Exceptions: records signed off as not an issue or an accepted risk, with the reason.
Resolution, reason, who signed off and when. Reopen puts a record back to fix.
People lists owners and stewards with their open work, approvals waiting, overdue and SLA.
The Unassigned row holds the open records nobody owns, so the total matches Work.
Open a person for their objects, open work and their own activity.
Balance work: even counts, whole objects, or by the assignment template.
Propose a plan, read the moves, apply it. The notice has Undo.
Data contracts: what each consumer is promised, and whether it is met.
A contract has versions and breaches; a data owner approves it, never their own.
Out of office: who covers your approvals and work between two dates.
Triage and SLA: days to resolve by severity, and the escalation chain.
The inbox: approvals, SLA warnings, finished runs, mentions and digests.
Each item has one action; mark read when you are done.
A run is one measurement of your data. Runs lists them on a timeline.
The baseline is marked: comparisons measure against it.
The table counts its own rows: 9 runs, 1 of them failed. Each run: system, trigger, records, rules, score range, status and duration.
A failed run says so; its job says why.
Jobs lists every extraction, analysis and configuration load.
Open a failed job for its stages, the error in plain words and Retry.
Start a run opens the start panel for an extraction or an analysis.
Choose the system and what to run.
Administration, Start and schedule starts and schedules extractions, analyses and uploads. The runs themselves are here on Runs.
One run: what it scored, object by object, and the jobs that made it.
15 objects scored: 2 go, 2 at risk, 11 no-go.
Measured, then the score shown after the cap.
Pin as baseline, archive older runs, download the report, or compare.
Compare: two runs side by side.
The method is stated: the common set of rules, and what counts as a change.
By object: measured before and after, the change, and rules new, fixed, worse and better.
What changed: the rules newly failing, fixed, worse and better.
On an object, Why the score moved says what the cap did.
The shown score moved only 69.8 to 70.0, because the cap holds it at 70.0.
Setup only reads from SAP; nothing is written until an approved batch is sent. Connect a system here.
Choose the system type and fill in the connection, then test it.
You can connect now and test later. Nothing is read until you extract.
The system canvas: health, type, last extraction and the last connection test.
Test, load or extract opens the system inspector.
Choose the objects and the scope, then a dry run counts what an extraction would read.
Configuration: what Meridian read from the customising tables, by area.
A table that could not be read says why, and what the user needs.
Schedules: full or changes only, on a rhythm, times in UTC.
Custom objects: Z tables and fields found across every system, with anomalies.
Connection settings: stored secrets are never shown; type new values to replace them.
A golden record is the one trusted version of a thing held more than once.
Match candidates, best score first, each with Review.
Review opens the pair side by side: pick a value per field that differs.
Merge the pair, or mark it not a duplicate with the reason.
Golden records: sources, survivorship, confidence, last merged and open conflicts.
Open conflicts are fields where the sources disagree and no rule has settled it.
Survivorship rules decide, field by field, which value survives.
Most recent, most complete, most frequent, trusted source, chain of systems, manual override.
Save the rules; they apply at the next match run.
Every merge and every not a duplicate is in the audit log.
The glossary: one business term per SAP field.
Each term has a definition, its field, the owner, the status and the rules that cite it.
Under review means a data owner has not approved it yet.
Fields without a term: read by failing rules, with no term yet.
Add terms from the rule library drafts them; the owner approves each.

point.text: Add terms from the rule library

steps.caption: Open a term for its fields, rules, review cycle and history.
A data owner edits and approves a term. Mark as reviewed keeps an active term current.
Each term cites the rules that read its field, so the definition and the check agree.
Search finds a term by its name, its definition or its SAP field.
The glossary is per object: every object has its own tab.
Lineage draws why a failing value matters.
From the source table, to the field, to the rule, to the S/4 feature it blocks.
Hover or focus a node to read its facts.
Features come from the impact model of the current run.
Export as SVG for a slide or a document.
Related objects in the header: fix the upstream one first.
The lineage draws the failing rules with the highest value at risk, so the drawing stays readable.
The same features appear on the Readiness tab: blocked and degraded in S/4HANA.
Each feature names the rules behind it, so you know which fix releases it.
Open a feature to read what it does and which records hold it back.
Processes shows which business process steps this object's data blocks.
2 of 4 process steps are blocked by Material master: PTP step 3, PP step 1.
A blocked step names the activity, the field, its pass rate and failing records.
What if these rules were fixed: tick rules and see which steps would be ready.
Nothing is changed and no data is read.
Open a step to hand its blocking rule to a steward.
The process designer: the model, its levels, and the fields each activity reads.
Save as a new version, then publish. The Processes tab shows it on the next run.
Versions keep every saved model with what changed.
Reports are built from stored runs, so a number in a report matches the run it names.
Every report: its run, format, who made it and the download.
Schedules build a report from the latest run and send it.
Open a schedule: report, which run, cadence, recipients.
Run it now, pause, or delete. Files already made stay in the list.
Create a report from any run.
Choose the report and the run it is built from.
Reports come from a run: the board pack, the analyst workbook, the analysis and trend reports, the rule catalogue.
A schedule that partly delivered or failed says so in Last result.
Channels that can take reports are set under Administration, Alerts.
A wave is a set of objects moved together in one cutover.
Each wave: due date, go, at risk and no-go counts, and the gate state.
The next step follows the nearest wave.
Edit opens the migration waves panel.
Name, target date and stage: plan, mock loads, dress rehearsal, cutover.
The gate: min score, zero criticals, contracts met, each with what fails it now.
The readiness certificate is not signed in this version; its link shows the checks.
Assign each object to a wave, then save the changes.
Administration: everything that sets up this tenant.
Users: seats, roles as grants, invitations.
Roles and permissions: built-in roles are fixed; copy one to change it.
Single sign-on with OpenID Connect, and the sign-in page rules.
View as a role: read-only, for support, and in the audit log.
Licence: status, seats, validity and the modules this deployment may use.
Settings: weights, score bands, the cap rule and tolerance, cost model and retention.
One critical rule beyond its tolerance holds an object at 85; two or more at 70. The caps are fixed.
Stewardship: one owner per object, stewards per slice, and the gaps.
Configuration bundle: export the configuration as one file; import with a diff first.
Rules import and export: imported rules land as drafts, never live.
Audit log: every change, by whom and when, and every call to the language model.
Alerts: channels and thresholds. Alerts never carry record values.
Default digest: the summary the tenant gets by default. Each person sets their own in Preferences.
Start and schedule: start an extraction, an analysis, a configuration load or an upload, and schedule them.
Platform and updates: jobs, the platform version, health checks and the diagnostics bundle.
Preferences belong to you, not the tenant. Every change is saved at once.
Theme and row density.
Number and date format, and your time zone. The sample line shows the result.
Start screen: open Meridian as another role's start screen. Your access does not change.
Keyboard hints, your digest, and critical findings at once.
What you hear about: the events that reach your inbox.
Out of office is set from People: who covers your approvals while you are away.
Inbox and triage settings decide what reaches your inbox and who covers it.
Your digest: daily, weekly or off.
Preferences open from your account menu, top right.
Meridian can be driven from the keyboard. Question mark shows every shortcut.
The shortcut sheet: everywhere, go to, tables, the ledger, the inspector, the command line.
Esc closes the top layer.
Command K, or slash, opens the command line.
Type a rule id to open the rule.

fill.label: Search, ask, or type a command

steps.caption: Or a word such as approve.

fill.label: Search, ask, or type a command

steps.caption: Enter opens it.
G then W goes to Work; g then l, r or p to Landscape, Runs or People.
In the ledger, j and k move, x selects, Enter opens the row.
a accepts the suggested value, n marks not an issue, r accepts the risk, e exports the fix sheet.
In the inspector, the square brackets step to the previous and next row.
Programme lead: how ready is each system and object for the next wave?
Step 1, Landscape: read the sentence and press the next step for your nearest wave.
Step 2, Waves: open the wave and set its gate.
Min score, zero criticals, contracts met. Save the gate.
Step 3, an object: read why it is no-go. Measured, capped, by which rules.
Step 4, People: who holds the open work. Balance it if one person holds most.
Step 5, Reports: schedule the board pack for the steering committee.
Share any page as a read-only link from Share and export.
Watch an object to hear about runs, score drops and new critical breaches.
Data steward: decide the right value for each failing field.
Step 1, Landscape: press Accept the suggested values.
Step 2, Work: your rows, ranked by value at risk.
Accept a suggested value; the notice has Undo.
Step 3, a record: read the possible values and type the new value.
Step 4, By rule: decide a whole rule at once, or export the fix sheet.
By rule groups the rows to fix under their rule.
Step 5, Waiting for approval: your batch waits for a data owner.
Data owner: you are accountable for your objects, and the second pair of eyes.
Step 1, Landscape: how many batches wait for you, and your SLA.
Step 2, the batch: the changes and the approval trail. Approve or send back.
Step 3, Waiting for approval: every batch, grouped.
Step 4, your object: watch it, and apply the steward template.
Step 5, Out of office: who covers your approvals while you are away.
Contracts: approve them, never your own.
Exceptions: records signed off as not an issue or an accepted risk, with the reason.
Triage and SLA: the days to resolve and the escalation chain after a breach.
SAP Basis: connections, extractions, schedules and jobs.
Step 1, the Basis home: each connection and what its last test said.
The last extraction of each system with its records, and whether it was analysed.
Failed jobs to triage, and the authorisation errors among the tests and jobs.
The extraction schedules, with the next run and the mode.
Step 2, the system: test the connection.
Step 3, the inspector: choose objects, dry run, then extract or extract changes only.
Step 4, Schedules: Changes only for routine runs.
Step 5, Runs: open a failed job and retry it.
Field mappings and Start and schedule are under Administration.
Configuration: what was read from the customising tables, and what could not be read and why.
Custom objects: Z tables and fields, with anomalies to investigate.
Process analyst: read the data through the business process.
Step 1, Landscape: press Open PTP step 3.
Step 2, Processes: which steps Material master blocks, and the fields behind them.
Step 3, What if: tick the rules to fix and see which steps would be ready.
Step 4, the step: hand its blocking rule to a steward.
Step 5, the designer: map the fields each activity reads, then publish.
A step is blocked when a field it writes fails a critical or high rule, or passes under 70%.
Comment on a rule from its inspector to tell the steward what the process needs.
Related objects in the header show which object to fix first.
Auditor and viewer: read every number and its receipt. Nothing you do changes data.
Step 1, Landscape: the same landscape, read-only.
Step 2, an object: the receipt and every i.
Step 3, Approvals: the four-eyes evidence.
Step 4, Audit log: filter by person and dates, then export.
Step 5, a person's activity.
A share link opens one page read-only, as a viewer.
Every comparison states its method: the common set of rules and what counts as a change.
A rule's versions and history sit side by side in its inspector.
Administrator: set the tenant up and keep it right.
Step 1, Users: invite people and give each a role.
Step 2, Single sign-on: connect your identity provider and test it.
Step 3, Settings: weights, bands, cap rule and tolerance, cost model, retention.
Step 4, Stewardship: owners and stewards, check the diff, apply, close the gaps.
Step 5, Platform and updates: health checks and the platform version.
Support: copy the diagnostics from help. They hold no record values and no secrets.
View as a role: see the product as one role sees it, read-only, for support.
Configuration bundle: move a configuration between tenants, with a diff first.
A clean is never one-off. After a batch loads, the next run shows which records failed again.
Per system: the score before and after the batch, records failing again and records fixed since.
Failing again by week, against the records fixed. A rising line means the source keeps creating bad data.

point.text: Failing again and fixed, by week

steps.caption: Drift by rule names the rules that come back, so the fix goes upstream to the process, not the record.
Still clean by batch: each loaded batch with the records that stayed fixed.
Ask Meridian answers questions about your data from this run's facts only.
Open it from the top bar on any screen.
Start from a suggested question or type your own.

point.text: What is holding the score down?

steps.caption: Every number in the answer must match a fact. If one does not, the answer is withheld.

click.text: What is holding the score down?

steps.caption: The facts used and the rules cited sit under the answer, so you can check each figure.
